# Banks and Credit Unions

![Print icon](/assets/home/images/global/print.png)

# Banks and Credit Unions

With your new IDNYC Card, you can open a bank or credit union account at one of several financial institutions across New York City.

The banks and credit unions listed below accept IDNYC as a primary form of ID to open an account.

Depending on the policies of the financial institution, you may be required to provide additional documentation such as proof of address, Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), or a small initial deposit. Credit unions have additional membership requirements.

You can also learn more about opening a bank account at one of the City's [Financial Empowerment Centers](http://www1.nyc.gov/site/dca/consumers/get-free-financial-counseling.page) operated by the Department of Consumer Affairs, where you can schedule free one-on-one financial counseling sessions in English or Spanish.

The appearance of any financial institution on this list does not constitute an endorsement by the IDNYC Program or the City of New York. The listing is provided as a convenience for persons who are looking for institutions that accept IDNYC as a primary form of ID to open an account.

### IDNYC Financial Brochure

This multi-language brochure explains the advantages of opening a bank or credit union account, and lists the financial institutions that accept IDNYC as primary identification when opening an account. The brochure is written in English, Spanish (Español), Chinese (简化字), Russian (Русский язык), Haitian Creole (Kreyòl Ayisyen), Korean (한국어), and Arabic (العربية).

# Benefits

![Print icon](/assets/home/images/global/print.png)

# Benefits

Your IDNYC card is a broadly accepted, official form of identification. IDNYC is accepted:

Your IDNYC card also offers a wide variety of exciting benefits that make it more than just an ID card. Your card can help you experience everything New York has to offer.

For your convenience, we have included information from our benefit providers. For the most accurate and up-to-date information about these benefits or if you have any questions about accessing them, please contact the organizations listed below. IDNYC is **not** responsible for determining your access to these benefits.

Click a topic, or press the enter key on a topic, to reveal more information.

Latest IDNYC Benefits

We're always working to make IDNYC better. Visit the Latest IDNYC Benefits page to find out more about the newest IDNYC card benefits below.

Museums and Cultural Institutions

IDNYC cardholders are now eligible for free one-year memberships at over 35 participating institutions. [Visit the Museums and Cultural Institutions page](/site/idnyc/benefits/museums-and-cultural-institutions.page "Visit the Museums and Cultural Institutions page") to find out more about the Museums and Cultural Institutions.

Banks and Credit Unions

With your IDNYC Card, you can open a bank or credit union account at one of several financial institutions across New York City. [Visit the Banks and Credit Unions page](/site/idnyc/benefits/banks-and-credit-unions.page "Visit the Banks and Credit Unions page") to find out more about the Banks and Credit Unions below.

Entertainment Discounts

With your IDNYC card, you will have access to exclusive entertainment discounts in New York City and nationwide. [Visit the Entertainment Discounts page](/site/idnyc/benefits/entertainment-discounts.page "Visit the Entertainment Discounts page") to find out more about the Entertainment Discounts below.

Housing

Your IDNYC is the only ID card you need for affordable housing through NYC Housing Connect. With IDNYC, you don't need a driver’s license, social security card or birth certificate to be eligible for housing on Housing Connect. Visit the [Housing page](https://www1.nyc.gov/site/idnyc/benefits/housing.page) to learn more.

Health

With your IDNYC card you can access benefits to help you stay healthy! [Visit the Health page](/site/idnyc/benefits/health-benefits.page "Visit the Health page") to find out more about the IDNYC card health benefits listed below.

Fitness

With your IDNYC card, you can stay fit in every borough. [Visit the Fitness page](/site/idnyc/benefits/fitness-benefits.page "Visit the Fitness page") to learn more about the benefits listed below.

Sporting Events

With your IDNYC card, you can get discounts on the hottest sporting events with discounts. [Visit the Sporting Events page](/site/idnyc/benefits/sporting-events.page "Visit the Sporting Events page") to learn more about the benefits listed below.

Transportation and Car Rental

With your IDNYC card, you can travel across all five boroughs! [Visit the Transportation and Car Rental page](/site/idnyc/benefits/transportation.page "Visit the Transportation page") to learn more about the benefits listed below.

Education

With your IDNYC card, you and your kids can learn just about anything with discounted classes. [Visit the Education page](/site/idnyc/benefits/education.page "Visit the Educational page") to learn more about the benefits listed below.

Teens & Young Adults

Use your IDNYC card to enjoy your city! [Visit the Teens & Young Adults page](/site/idnyc/benefits/teen-young-adults.page "Visit the Teens and Young Adults page") to learn more about the benefits listed below.

Libraries

You can use your IDNYC card at any public library in New York City. [Visit the Libraries page](/site/idnyc/benefits/libraries.page "Visit the Libraries page") to learn more about each library below.

The IDNYC U.S. Veteran Designation

If you are a U.S. Veteran you can have "Veteran" printed on the front of your IDNYC card. [Visit the IDNYC U.S. Veteran Designation page](/site/idnyc/benefits/veteran-designation.page "Visit the IDNYC U.S. Veteran Designation page") to learn more about the organizations below that accept the designation as proof of veteran status.

# Enrollment Help

The Office of Student Enrollment (OSE) is here to help families through the process of enrolling students into a NYC Public School. We provide guidance on school options, admissions requirements and application timelines to ensure families understand their school options. We’re here to support parents and guardians with transfers, special programs, and language services so every family can find the right school for their child.

## What Can We Help You With?

[Family Welcome Centers](/enrollment/enrollment-help/family-welcome-centers)

[Find a School](https://schoolsearch.schools.nyc/)

![Illustration of dad and daughter at a desk talking to enrollment](https://pwsblobprd.schools.nyc/prd-pws/images/default-source/default-album/enrollment/enrollment-help/fwc-family-chat.svg?sfvrsn=99b1aed6_8 "Enrollment Help for Parent and Child")

## Enrollment Help Information

Find helpful enrollment information on key topics below. Whether you’re a new family, need to transfer schools, or are exploring home schooling, these resources can guide you through each step. You can also learn about Family Welcome Centers and access enrollment forms.

## Meeting Student Enrollment Needs

NYC Public Schools are committed to providing excellent educational opportunities that are open, accessible, and welcoming to all of the city's students. Section below contains information about specific student needs like LGBTQ, diversity and disability needs.

## Family Welcome Centers

Family Welcome Centers support families enrolling in NYC Public Schools with specific enrollment needs. Visit the FWC page to find our more about the specific enrollment services that Family Welcome Centers provide. Whether you prefer to meet in person, talk by phone, or connect virtually, our staff is here to help with specific enrollment needs.

[Family Welcome Centers](/enrollment/enrollment-help/family-welcome-centers)

![Illustration of dad and daughter at a desk talking to enrollment](https://pwsblobprd.schools.nyc/prd-pws/images/default-source/default-album/enrollment/enrollment-help/fwc-family-chat.svg?sfvrsn=99b1aed6_8 "Enrollment Help for Parent and Child")

## Contact Us

If you need to contact us in regards to enrollment support, you can email the Office of Student Enrollment at the email addresses below.

Use this email for 3-K, Pre-K, Kindergarten, Gifted and Talented enrollment help and school offers

[ESEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:ESEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov)

Use this email for 6th to 8th Grade enrollment help including middle school offers

[MSEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:MSEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov)

Use this email for 9th to 12th Grade enrollment help including high school offers

[HSEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov](mailto:HSEnrollment@schools.nyc.gov)

Call Monday-Friday, 8am-6pm at 718-935-2009.

## Technology for families

### Students

Access all your DOE applications – TeachHub, Google, iLearnNYC, Microsoft Office, Zoom, and more–from one place.

### SupportHub

Need technical support? Visit the SupportHub for answers to common questions and to open a support ticket.

### NYC Schools Account (NYCSA)

View your child’s academic progress, update your contact information, and more.

### Parent University

Parent University seeks to educate and empower families through free courses, resources, events, and activities.

### MySchools

Apply to grades 3-K –12, explore and compare schools, and more.

# Project Open Arms

![](https://pwsblobprd.schools.nyc/prd-pws/images/default-source/building-accessibility/nycps-web-header-poa-3.png?sfvrsn=5523aa15_3)

## Welcome

[Project Open Arms](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/home/downloads/pdf/press-releases/2022/OpenArms-Families-Seeking-Asylum.pdf) supports immigrant families including those seeking [asylum](https://help.unhcr.org/usa/applying-for-asylum/what-is-asylum/) and ensures children are provided a full range of services. This multi-agency coordination highlights wraparound services to ensure immigrant families and their children will have access to critical academic, social-emotional, and language-based supports needed to be successful in New York City Public Schools.

**The mission of Project Open Arms**for NYC Public Schools is to coordinate efforts of all divisions in NYCPS to support our newest New Yorkers successfully.

## A Message from our Chancellor

Below is a letter from our Chancellor regarding New York City Public Schools reassurance for immigrant families that schools are safe, supportive environments and the various legal and community resources for help with any immigration‑related concerns.

**September 2026: Immigrant Support Letter**

### Available In

### Know Your Rights Resources

**Know Your Rights Comic book:** New York City is—and always will be—a city for all immigrants. It is important that New Yorkers, including undocumented immigrants, know their rights. This comic presents a series of vignettes that illustrate the rights and protections available to all New Yorkers. It is our hope that these stories will help educate community members and prepare individuals for potential encounters with non-local law enforcement officers, including the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). After the comic, there are pages with links and resources to help individuals learn more about their rights in New York City. These resources can help address questions you or people you know might have. You can access the comic on WeTeach using this [link](https://www.weteachnyc.org/resources/collection/know-your-rights-comic/).

**Know Your Rights Flyer:** This resource, in partnership with the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA), serves as a reminder that NYC Public Schools **does not ask about or track immigration status**, student information is protected by strict privacy rules. All families have the right to **free translation services** and to **safe, welcoming schools where immigration enforcement cannot enter without a judicial warrant**. In this flyer parents are encouraged to keep emergency contacts updated and explore **caregiver designation options** to ensure children are cared for during unexpected situations. Below you can access this flyer in various languages.

**Know Your Rights Flyer**

### Available In

#### MOIA’s Know Your Rights Booklets

The NYC Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs has created Know Your Rights booklets in multiple languages to share information and resources, that can be found [Know Your Rights booklets page](https://www.nyc.gov/site/immigrants/legal-resources/know-your-rights.page) along with other resources.

## Upcoming Events

Coming soon.

## TPS and Federal Updates

*Updated as of January 5, 2026, this general information is not legal advice and may change due to future announcements
or litigation.*[Temporary Protected Status](https://www.nyc.gov/site/immigrants/legal-resources/temporary-protected-status.page)
 (TPS) allows individuals from certain countries to remain in the United States if it is unsafe for them to return
to their home country due to a humanitarian emergency there. Some announcements about TPS from the federal government
may impact the status of many in our schools, leaving them with questions about their own immigration status.
Constituents with questions should call the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA) Immigration Legal Support Hotline
at 800-354-0365 for information on how and where to find City-funded, free, and safe immigration legal help.
Additionally, if a NYCPS student or family member has questions regarding immigration supports, they should reach out to
their school principal. We would also like to highlight updated MOIA resources:

## Supports

### Legal Supports

The Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA) provides the following information and services to support immigrant New
Yorkers navigate the U.S. immigration system and build their lives and futures in New York. Families can call the
City-funded, free, and safe MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365, or call 311 and say, "Immigration
Legal," between 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Friday, to get:

Please note that the MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline does not schedule people for legal appointments directly.
If families would like information on how to find a provider that speaks your language and is geographically
close to them, please call 800-354-0365 or visit MOIA’s website which lists MOIA’s current partners:

[MOIA Legal Resources page](https://www.nyc.gov/site/immigrants/legal-resources/legal-resources.page)

Schools may also wish to share these additional publicly available resources for families looking for legal
assistance.     

[New Americans page](https://dos.ny.gov/office-new-americans)[Immigration Advocates page](https://www.immigrationadvocates.org/legaldirectory/search?state=NY)[NYCourts.gov 'Find a Lawyer' Resource](https://www.nycourts.gov/courthelp/GoingToCourt/findlawyer.shtml)[City Bar Justice Center Legal hotline](https://www.citybarjusticecenter.org/legal-hotline/)

### Health Supports

Did you know your child has 30 days to complete their vaccinations in order to attend school? If a student is new to
the country/state, is living in temporary housing, AND has an upcoming appointment, there is also an extended grace
period (90 days).

More information may be found on the
[immunizations page](/school-life/health-and-wellness/immunizations)
.

#### The links below show primary care clinics in all boroughs that provide required vaccinations at no cost to families.

### Basic Needs Supports

[Care Closets](https://www.instagram.com/reel/CqazOBXgE6z/?igshid=YmMyMTA2M2Y%3D)
(click the link to see what they look like!) are created in your child's school to provide basic necessities that your
family may need. Such as, school supplies, clothing, non-perishable food, hygiene products and much more. You can work
with your parent coordinator to schedule a time to discuss what needs you may have or to visit their care closet!

Food Pantries: View
[the list of local food pantry locations](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dycd/services/food_pantries.page)
to find a pantry near you. Contact individual pantries to confirm schedule.

### Mental Health Supports

Call or text 
[NYC Well](https://nyc988.cityofnewyork.us/en/)
at 988.

### Special Education Supports

[Special Education Family Resources](/learning/special-education/family-resources)
-

## Our Partners

## FAQ's

### Does NYC Public School ask families for their countries of origin or their immigration status?

We do NOT ask families about country of origin or asylum-seeking status.

### Can families only utilize the enrollment center in their borough where they live?

Families can visit any Family Welcome Center throughout the city. Enrollment Staff is here to assist and enroll
students regardless of their district.​

### When can students enroll for school?

Family Welcome Centers enroll students year-round, just as schools do, typically as soon as they arrive at our office.
Our goal is to make the enrollment process smooth and accessible.​

### Do families need an enrollment letter to enroll in their zoned elementary or middle school?

Families do not need an enrollment assignment letter to register at their zoned elementary or middle school. In fact,
they can go directly to their zoned school with proper registration documents.​

# Family Welcome Centers (FWCs)

FWCs support families enrolling in NYC Public Schools with specific enrollment needs. Parents and guardians can schedule a virtual or in-person appointment at any location to get help with school enrollment. FWCs are open Monday - Thursday from 8am - 5pm, and Friday from 8am - 3pm.

![Illustration of dad and daughter at a desk talking to enrollment](https://pwsblobprd.schools.nyc/prd-pws/images/default-source/default-album/enrollment/enrollment-help/fwc-family-chat.svg?sfvrsn=99b1aed6_8)

## Services

Family Welcome Centers provide specific services. If your child has a zoned school or received an offer from a school through the admissions process, you need to contact that school directly for enrollment help. Family Welcome Centers can offer specific enrollment services which are listed below.

Get help enrolling a student in a NYC public school, whether new, returning, or switching from a charter or private school, and submit required documents online.

Get help transferring a student from one NYC public school to another. This includes travel hardship transfers for high school students.

Get assistance with exploring schools, applying, and checking waitlist status in MySchools.

## Book an Appointment

Before visiting, please review the information below.

You will need to provide ID and enrollment documentation during your meeting. Review the list of accepted documents on our Registration Checklist. Be prepared to provide this information electronically for virtual appointments.

[Enrollment Forms](/enrollment/enrollment-help/enrollment-forms)

Our office cannot make changes to the application or waitlist process. If you would like to explore other school options, you must add your child to the waitlists of other desired schools through your MySchools account.

[MySchools](https://www.myschools.nyc/)

New and returning elementary or middle school students do not need to visit our office. You can find your zoned school using our Find a School tool, and enroll directly at the school.

[Find a School](https://schoolsearch.schools.nyc/)

If you cannot find an appointment that works for you, please call 718-935-2828 for assistance in finding a date and time that work for you.

# Please Note

If you have a zoned school, you should seek enrollment help directly at that school. Visit the site below and type in your address to find your zoned school. If you are interested in a school other than your zoned school, schedule an appointment.

[Find a School](https://schoolsearch.schools.nyc/)

If your child needs support, contact their school or email the Office of Student Enrollment based on the admissions process.

[Find a School](https://schoolsearch.schools.nyc/)

# QPL’s Special Edition Hip Hop Card

Celebrate Hip Hop's 50th Anniversary with this special edition library card!

Hip Hop was born in NYC in 1973. Fifty years later, it's a global force for culture, civil rights, AND music**.**

We're celebrating Hip Hop's 50th Anniversary with **our Special Edition Hip Hop Card**, featuring art by the legendary street-wear trailblazers, **the Shirt Kings!**

QPL’s Special Edition Hip Hop Card is **available at all Queens Public Library locations**, while supplies last.

[Show us how much you love your new card!](https://www.instagram.com/stories/highlights/18090617896349089/) Post pictures on your social media channels **using the hashtag #QPLHipHopCard.**

Do it for the culture! Show the world that Hip Hop is here to stay—with your Special Edition Hip Hop Card!

### QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card FAQs

**Where can I get QPL’s Special Edition Hip Hop Card?**  
 You can get the card **at any Queens Public Library location**, while supplies last. See a list of QPL locations here: <https://queenslibrary.org/about-us/locations>

The QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card is **limited to one (1) card per customer/library account.**

The QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card **can only be used at Queens Public Library locations.** It will not work at the New York Public Library, Brooklyn Public Library, or any other library system in New York.

**What is the significance of the artwork on the card?**  
 The Special Edition Hip Hop Card features art by street-wear pioneers the [Shirt Kings](http://www.shirtkingphade.com/). Starting in 1986 from a booth at the Colosseum Mall in Jamaica, Queens, their graffiti-inspired custom clothing designs were embraced by some of the biggest names in Hip Hop. Shirt Kings designs were also featured on album covers and in music videos, and they helped lay the foundation for Hip Hop fashion across the world. Our card reflects the Shirt Kings’ trademark style, while reinforcing the importance of reading, writing, positivity, and fun!

**Can anyone of any age get the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card?**  
 Yes, anyone of any age who [meets the criteria](https://www.queenslibrary.org/help/faq?id=76) for a QPL card can get this card, while supplies last.

**I am a current QPL cardholder. Can I still get the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card?**  
 Yes, current cardholders can get the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card at no cost. All you need to do is bring your photo ID to a QPL location and speak with a QPL staff member. You can keep your old card as a souvenir or return it to a QPL staff member. Your old card will be deactivated.

**I do not live in Queens. Can I still get the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card?**  
 Yes. You must live, work, go to school, or own property in New York to receive a free QPL card. If you live out of state, you must pay a $50 fee.

**I received my QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card at the Hip Hop 50 Summit or another event. How do I activate my card?**  
 You can activate your card by visiting the QPL Bookmobile or by coming to any QPL location. If you are an existing QPL cardholder, please bring your photo ID. If you are a new QPL cardholder, please bring your photo ID and proof of your name and address. A QPL staff member will activate your card appropriately. For more details about valid photo identification and proof of name and address, visit here: <https://queenslibrary.org/verifying-identity>

**I got a [QPL Special Edition Mets Library Card](https://www.queenslibrary.org/mets) earlier this year. Can I also get a Hip Hop Card?**  
 Yes, you can get a Hip Hop Card, but please note: **after the Hip Hop Card is activated, it will be your only QPL card.** Any other QPL card that you have (including the Mets Library Card) will be deactivated. You can keep your Mets Library Card as a souvenir.

**I use an IDNYC Card as my library card. Can I still get the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card?**  
 Yes, you will need to bring your photo ID to a QPL location and speak with a QPL staff member. Once you activate your QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card, your IDNYC card will no longer work as a QPL card. You can still use your IDNYC card at other cultural institutions, the New York Public Library, and Brooklyn Public Library.

**There is a long line at my QPL location to get a QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card. Is there any way I can make this process quicker?**  
 If you are a current QPL cardholder, you will need to wait to speak to a QPL staff member – please have your photo ID ready. If you are a new cardholder, you can start the process by completing an e-card registration form online. Then, show your confirmation email, along with your proof of address, to a QPL staff member. The e-card registration form can be found here: <https://queenslibrary.org/get-a-card/eUser>

**How long will the QPL Special Edition Hip Hop Card be available?**  
 The card will be available while supplies last. There are limited quantities at each QPL location.
